hero.headline: Your media. Your library. Your Phlix.
hero.subheadline: An open-source PHP media server that streams to your Roku, Samsung TV, Windows desktop, phone, and any DLNA device — with SyncPlay, Live TV, transcoding, and a hub that follows you anywhere.

pitch_bullets: 100% self-hostable — your library never leaves your hardware unless you say so
Native apps for Roku, Samsung Tizen, Windows, Mobile, and the Linux console — plus the web portal and any DLNA device
Real-time SyncPlay with NTP-style time sync so movie night actually stays in sync
Multi-source metadata: TMDB, TVDB, Fanart.tv, and local NFO with 24-hour cache
Adaptive HLS streaming, FFmpeg transcoding, per-device quality profiles
Live TV with DVR + EPG guide integration
Plugin system with a versioned manifest contract

features.title: Library that organizes itself
features.body: Add a file, see it appear. Phlix watches your folders for changes, recognizes naming like S01E02 and (2020), and fills in the titles, descriptions, and artwork for you — no renaming rituals, no manual entry.

features.title: SyncPlay across the room or across the country
features.body: Watch together, perfectly in step. Phlix keeps every device's playback clock tightly synced, so play, pause, and seek move together for everyone in the room — or an ocean away.

features.title: Transcoding that picks the right quality
features.body: Every device gets the right quality on its own — dedicated profiles for phones, web, and 4K TVs. When a file won't play directly, Phlix transcodes it on the fly with FFmpeg (H.264 defaults to CRF 23, the sweet spot between quality and size) and delivers it as adaptive HLS that rides out network hiccups. If your server has a compatible Intel or AMD GPU, hardware profiles run the heavy work on it instead of the CPU.

features.title: Multi-user, multi-profile, parental controls
features.body: One account, up to 5 personal profiles by default, each lockable with a 4- or 6-digit PIN. Passwords are protected with Argon2ID — today's strongest widely recommended hashing — and sign-ins stay secure with tokens that refresh themselves. Rating filters from G to NC-17 keep kids' profiles to kids' content. Bring your existing identity too: OIDC, LDAP, and passkeys all work, so Phlix fits the sign-in you already run.

features.title: Live TV with DVR + EPG
features.body: Watch, pause, and record live TV. Schedule a recording once and it happens on time; the on-screen guide opens straight to what's on now — no clicking through menus.

features.title: DLNA for the devices you already own
features.body: Phlix speaks DLNA — the streaming standard already built into most older smart TVs, game consoles, and receivers — so the devices you own can play your library with no app to install.

features.title: Plugin system with a real contract
features.body: Install plugins straight from Settings → Plugins and switch them on — Trakt and Last.fm keep your watch history in step on services you already use (that's what scrobbling means), extra metadata providers sharpen artwork and subtitles, and more add-ons ship every month. Want to build your own? A versioned contract and a minimal starter repo (phlix-plugin-example) show you the way in.

features.title: Phlix Hub — reach any of your servers from anywhere
features.body: The hub is a small server you run in the cloud that connects your devices to your home server — no ports to open, no third-party tunnel. Sign in once and watch your library from anywhere. You run the hub, you own the relay. Hubs can even link up with each other, each proving its identity with an Ed25519 signature.

faq.q: Is Phlix like Plex / Jellyfin / Emby?
faq.a: Yes — same job, different stack. Phlix is built in PHP 8.3+ on Workerman, ships with a versioned plugin contract, and includes a hub for accessing remote servers behind NAT without a third-party tunnel.

faq.q: Do I need to expose my server to the internet?
faq.a: No. Run Phlix on your LAN and use the Phlix Hub's reverse-tunnel relay to reach it from your phone or Roku at a friend's house. You can self-host the hub..
Anything FFmpeg can read. Direct play when the client supports it; transcoded HLS otherwise. Per-device quality profiles pick the right bitrate automatically.
Yes — React Native, currently in beta. It is not in the App Store or Google Play yet — Android installs from the release APK on GitHub, and iOS is build-from-source today.
